title: Electrochemistry
description: Chemical reactions that make electricity, and electricity that drives reactions.

entries.name: Galvanic cells
entries.tagline: A cell that turns the energy of a redox reaction into electric current.

sections.text: A galvanic (or voltaic) cell has two half-cells. In one, a species is oxidized. In the other, a species is reduced. A wire carries the electrons between them, and that flow is the current.

points: Anode: the electrode where oxidation happens. It is the negative electrode in a galvanic cell.
Cathode: the electrode where reduction happens. It is the positive electrode.
Salt bridge: a tube of salt solution that lets ions move between the half-cells, to keep each side electrically neutral. Without it the current would stop at once.
Electrons flow through the wire from the anode to the cathode.

sections.text: The zinc electrode dissolves and copper plates onto the other electrode. The cell gives about 1.10 V under standard conditions.
Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) ‖ Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s). The anode is written on the left, the cathode on the right, and ‖ stands for the salt bridge.

quiz.q: In a galvanic cell, oxidation takes place at the…
What is the job of the salt bridge?
quiz.a: To let ions move so each half-cell stays neutral

entries.name: Standard reduction potentials
entries.tagline: A scale that ranks how strongly species pull on electrons.

sections.text: The standard reduction potential, E°, in volts, measures how much a species wants to be reduced. Values are measured against the standard hydrogen electrode, which is defined as 0 V.
Both potentials are the reduction values from the table. The half-reaction with the higher E° is the cathode.

points: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu has E° = +0.34 V. Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Zn has E° = −0.76 V.
Copper is the cathode and zinc is the anode: E°(cell) = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.
A positive E°(cell) means the reaction is spontaneous.
Do not multiply E° by the number of electrons when balancing. It is a potential, not an amount.
Strong oxidizing agents (such as F₂ and MnO₄⁻) have high positive E°. Strong reducing agents (such as Li and Na) have very negative E°.

quiz.q: A galvanic cell has E°(cell) = +1.10 V. The reaction is…

entries.name: The Nernst equation
entries.tagline: How cell voltage changes when concentrations are not standard.

sections.text: n is the number of electrons transferred, F is the Faraday constant, and Q is the reaction quotient.

sections.h: Link to free energy and K
sections.text: A positive cell potential means a negative ΔG, which means a spontaneous reaction.

points: As a galvanic cell runs, Q grows, E falls, and when Q reaches K, E becomes zero. A flat battery is a cell at equilibrium.
A concentration cell has the same species on both sides at different concentrations, and gives a voltage from the Nernst equation alone.
The pH meter relies on the same effect, with a voltage that depends on the hydrogen ion concentration.

entries.name: Quantitative electrolysis
entries.tagline: Calculating how much substance an electric current produces.

sections.text: One mole of electrons carries a charge of 96 485 coulombs. This is the Faraday constant, F.

equations: charge Q = current I × time t
moles of electrons = I × t ÷ F

sections.text: How much copper is deposited by 2.00 A running for 30.0 minutes through a Cu²⁺ solution?
points: Moles of electrons = 3600 ÷ 96 485 = 0.0373 mol.
Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu needs 2 mol of electrons per mole of copper, so 0.0187 mol of Cu forms.

quiz.q: What is the charge of one mole of electrons?

entries.name: Batteries
entries.tagline: Galvanic cells packaged to power things.

sections.text: A battery is one or more galvanic cells. Primary batteries are used once. Secondary (rechargeable) batteries have reactions that can be reversed by passing a current backwards.

facts: Zinc is the anode and manganese dioxide the cathode, in a basic electrolyte. About 1.5 V per cell.
Lead anode, lead(IV) oxide cathode, sulfuric acid electrolyte. About 2 V per cell, and six cells make a 12 V car battery.
Lithium ions move between a graphite anode and a metal oxide cathode. High energy for its weight, so it powers phones and electric cars. About 3.6–3.7 V per cell.

sections.text: A fuel cell is like a battery that is fed continuously with fuel. In a hydrogen fuel cell, hydrogen is oxidized at the anode and oxygen is reduced at the cathode, and the only product is water.

quiz.q: Which type of battery is used in most phones and electric cars?

entries.name: Corrosion and rusting
entries.tagline: Metals slowly returning to their ores, and how to stop it.

sections.text: Corrosion is the oxidation of a metal by its surroundings. Rusting of iron needs both oxygen and water, and is an electrochemical process.

points: At one spot on the surface iron is oxidized: Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ (an anode).
At another spot oxygen is reduced: O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻ (a cathode).
The Fe²⁺ is oxidized further and forms hydrated iron(III) oxide, the flaky red-brown rust.
Salt water speeds it up because the dissolved ions let the current flow more easily.
Paint or oil keeps out water and oxygen.
Galvanizing coats steel with zinc. Zinc is more reactive than iron, so even where the coating is scratched, the zinc corrodes first.
A sacrificial anode, a block of magnesium or zinc bolted to the steel, corrodes instead of the steel. Ship hulls and pipelines use them.
Stainless steel contains chromium, which forms a thin protective oxide layer.

quiz.q: How does a sacrificial anode protect steel?
quiz.a: It is more reactive and corrodes instead
wrong: It coats the steel in paint
It removes the oxygen from the air
It makes the steel less dense
